summary: Cetrimide is a quaternary ammonium cationic surfactant with antiseptic and disinfectant properties, used topically to clean and disinfect skin, minor wounds, burns and surfaces, and as a constituent of antiseptic creams and combination products (e.g., with chlorhexidine). It acts by disrupting microbial cell membranes. It is for external use only; it is not an FDA-approved systemic drug, and this record reflects EMA/SmPC and pharmacopeial/reference information.

moa: Cetrimide is a cationic quaternary ammonium surfactant. Its positively charged hydrophilic head and lipophilic tail adsorb to and disrupt the negatively charged lipid bilayer of microbial cell membranes, increasing permeability and causing leakage of intracellular contents and cell death. It is bactericidal mainly against Gram-positive organisms (less active against Gram-negatives, notably Pseudomonas) and has detergent/cleansing action. Its activity is reduced by organic matter and by anionic surfactants (soaps).

overdose: Topical overdose may cause local irritation or chemical burns; wash the area with water. Ingestion is serious - it can cause burning of the mouth and throat, nausea, vomiting, muscle weakness, CNS depression, and respiratory difficulty. Do not induce vomiting; give water or milk to dilute, protect the airway, and obtain urgent medical/poison-center care with supportive treatment.
